cells.tense: Right now the two streams are moving as one and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: gather your determination and hold the line
cells.ask: When a pull this week tries to tilt what the two of you chose, gather yourself and hold that line once — plainly, the way any direction worth keeping gets held.
cells.core:
A genuine connection is being made, and it is holding. Two streams meet and run as one, and the fairness stays because you notice when it tilts and you steer back. Nothing dramatic is required. The direction you picked defends itself because you keep picking it in small ways, mostly privately.

What grows this is holding the line under one real push. Not a test you set up — the actual drift that arrives this week, one tilt, one pull off course. When it comes, gather what you know and refuse it once. Say what the shared direction is, and stay there. That is the whole practice. What you get is momentum that belongs to both of you, not a truce that must be re-won every morning. It costs one uncomfortable moment.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the chosen direction honest by holding it under one real pull.
cells.verb: Choosing one connection and letting two directions run as one
cells.place: Where fairness is recalibrated and proportion restored

cells.tense: Soon the merge will be pulled toward a future nobody can write in yet.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Stop one step short of holding the shape harder — give what has already grown here one unhurried hour without you guarding it.
cells.core:
The connection is real, and it is being over-managed. You read the next bend before anyone has walked it, arrange what has not happened, steer two streams by anticipation. The bracing looks like care; it lands as pressure, and the other person starts to feel watched rather than met. Fairness tips when one person carries the worry for both.

What has already grown here is yours to enjoy. Let one afternoon go untended — no steering, no pre-arranging, no fixing the next thing — and rest in the fact that something good came out of this. Care that does not grip is what the other person can move toward. Growth without forcing is not growth without intention; it is direction held lightly. The cost of holding it this way is a stretch of not knowing, and the merge gets room.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Name every pull on you about this connection, then mark beside each whose voice it actually is — hold off on acting until the marks are done.
cells.core:
The merge is available, and you are not in it. Something is held at arm's length — not refused, just not entered — and the present keeps arriving without you. The decision that belongs to you has not been made, or was made and then quietly set aside. The pull to stay on the threshold is strong enough that it may not look like a pull.

What is yours to do is tell the voices apart. Some of the pulls on you are yours; some came from somewhere else and were carried until they felt like yours. Put them on paper and mark each one. The mark is the act. Knowing which is which does its own work — accurate perception lands without argument, and once it lands, one step toward the door becomes possible. No pushing into the place you have been avoiding; sort the pulls first.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing, and you would say nothing is happening.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: For someone stuck on the route you already found, say the three steps in order — the words only, then let them walk it without you.
cells.core:
The merge is running, and your part in it is not in the account you give. You are the one who notices when the balance tips and adjusts without announcing it; the connection stays fair because of moves you make quietly, and if someone asked, you would say the fairness just happened. It did not. You have been doing it, and the credit sits on the table.

Before all this steering, there was something simpler: you could see the way through and point at it. You still can. Someone on that road is stuck where you once were — say the three steps in the order you took them, and then let them walk it. Not advice; directions. Saying it settles the record back where it belongs.
